etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English monument, from Old French monument, from Latin monumentum (“memorial”), from monēre (“to remind”).

definitions.definition: A structure built for commemorative or symbolic reasons, or as a memorial; a commemoration.
An important site owned by the community as a whole.

quote.text: The cab pulled up in front of a tumbledown cheap ‘villa’ in an unfinished cheap neighbourhood, — the whole place a living monument of the defeat of the speculative builder.

quote.citation: 1961 October, “Talking of Trains: Last of the M.S.W.J.R.”, in Trains Illustrated, page 586:
quote.text: The line became a monument to his drive and imagination — and a hard training course for the future chief of the Great Central.

definitions.definition: An important burial vault or tomb.
A surveying reference point marked by a permanently fixed marker (a survey monument).
A pile of stones left by a prospector to claim ownership of ore etc. found in a mine.
(surveying) A natural or artificial object used as a reference point.

quote.citation: 1896, Auguste Brachet, Paget Toynbee, A Historical Grammar of the French Language (Clarendon Press series)‎[1], Clarendon Press, →LCCN, →OCLC, page 15:
quote.text: This linguistic fragment, rough as it may appear, is of the highest interest; for it is the first written monument of the French language, eleven hundred years old.

quote.citation: 2018 June 11, Jared Klein, Brian Joseph, Matthias Fritz, editors, Handbook of Comparative and Historical Indo-European Linguistics (Handbücher zur Sprach- und Kommunikationswissenschaft / Handbooks of Linguistics and Communication Science [HSK])‎[2], Walter de Gruyter GmbH & Co KG, →ISBN, →OCLC:
quote.text: Czech was long used as a written language also by the Slovaks; the earliest existing Slovak monument is the Žilina Town Book from the late 15th century

definitions.definition: (transitive) To mark or memorialize with a monument.
(transitive) To place a surveyor's monument at.

quote.citation: 1985, Input Formats and Specifications of the National Geodetic Survey Data Base, pages 3-8:
quote.text: Enter the year the marker was monumented. If the year cannot be determined , enter " UNK " .

quote.citation: 2009, Stephen V. Estopinal, A Guide to Understanding Land Surveys, page 91:
quote.text: Having chosen and monumented the initial point, the surveyor established the "principal meridian" by traversing north and south from the initial point.

quote.citation: 2012, T. J. Blachut, A. Chrzanowski, J. H. Saastamoinen, Urban Surveying and Mapping, page 69:
quote.text: The first-order network is usually monumented on the roofs of buildings; ground stations are used only in suburban districts.
